classification.difficultyReason: The source requires full reasoning for a numerical result and a general exterior-angle proof.

content.prompt: Provide full reasoning for both parts below.

spec.description: Triangle ABC with AC extended through C to D; B lies above AC. Angle arcs mark 45 degrees at A, 60 degrees at B and exterior angle a at C.
spec.mathematics: A, C and D are collinear in that order. The interior angles at A and B are 45 degrees and 60 degrees. The exterior angle BCD is a.
spec.answerVisibility: Only source givens and the unknown label appear in the question diagram.

answer.short: $a=105^{\circ}$. The interior angle at $C$ is $75^{\circ}$; supplementary angles give $a=180^{\circ}-75^{\circ}$.
answer.worked:
Angle sum of a triangle:
$$\begin{align*}\angle ACB&=180^{\circ}-45^{\circ}-60^{\circ}\\\angle ACB&=75^{\circ}\end{align*}$$
Angles on a straight line are supplementary:
$$\begin{align*}a&=180^{\circ}-75^{\circ}\\a&=105^{\circ}\end{align*}$$

spec.description: Triangle ABC with AC extended through C to D; arcs identify interior angle y at A, interior angle x at B and exterior angle a at C.
spec.mathematics: A, C and D are collinear in that order. The exterior angle at C is supplementary to the interior angle BCA.
spec.answerVisibility: The question diagram contains angle labels x, y and a without supplied proof or additional angle values.

answer.worked:
Angle sum of a triangle gives:
$$\angle BCA=180^{\circ}-x-y.$$
Angles on a straight line are supplementary:
$$\begin{align*}a&=180^{\circ}-\angle BCA\\a&=180^{\circ}-(180^{\circ}-x-y)\\a&=x+y\end{align*}$$
